candidate_profile.description: The candidate is well structured and commercially strong. They move quickly to the cost side, identify the gallon economics clearly, and explain the pricing distortion and cost-allocation issue well, with only slightly less polish than an excellent answer.
behaviour_rules: Open with a concise recap and explicitly state that rising sales with falling profit points toward a cost or pricing problem.
Ask focused questions on package pricing, unit economics, labor requirements, and cost allocation.
Structure the problem around revenue confirmation, direct cost differences, and overhead allocation.
Clearly identify that plastic gallons are more expensive because of both packaging material and higher-skill labor.
Explain that the gallon price is lower on a per-ounce basis even though the product is more expensive to produce.
Use the 60% gallon mix shift as evidence that the business is increasingly selling the wrong product at the wrong economics.
Recognize that factory costs are being averaged in a way that hides the true profitability of each package format.
Recommend a thorough activity-based costing review and repricing, with a strong but not perfectly polished final synthesis.

expected_issues: May be slightly less crisp than an excellent candidate when synthesizing the root cause into one decisive statement.
Could give more concrete detail on how the repricing and costing review should be sequenced.
expected_feedback_points: Strong and well-prioritized focus on the cost side.
Strong diagnosis of gallon packaging, labor, and pricing economics.
Strong explanation of why average cost allocation masks the problem.
Strong use of the product mix shift to explain worsening profits.
Strong recommendation to apply activity-based costing and reprice gallons.
To reach excellent level, make the final synthesis even tighter and more executive-ready.
